# Tagr

> Tagr is an open source, self hosted music metadata editor with a web UI. You point it at your
> music folders, it scans them into SQLite, and it gives you a three panel browser interface
> (folder tree, song list, metadata editor) to browse, filter, play and edit audio tags, writing
> them back to the real files on disk.

- License: AGPL-3.0-only
- Repository: https://github.com/suitux/Tagr
- Docker image: ghcr.io/suitux/tagr:latest (linux/amd64, linux/arm64)
- Live demo: https://tagr-demo.fly.dev/ (login demo / demo, read only)
- Stack: Next.js 16, React 19, Prisma + SQLite, node-taglib-sharp, WaveSurfer.js
- Support the author: https://buymeacoffee.com/suitux

## What it is for

Self hosters keep their music on a NAS or a home server and serve it with Jellyfin, Navidrome or
Plex. Those servers read the tags inside the audio files, so bad tags mean a broken library. The
usual tag editors (MusicBrainz Picard, Mp3tag, beets) are desktop or CLI tools that expect to run
on the same machine as the files, which is awkward when that machine is headless. Tagr runs on the
server itself and gives you a browser UI, on desktop and on a phone.

## Features

- Edit 40+ metadata fields inline: title, artist, album, year, genre, composer, BPM, lyrics, sort
  fields, catalog numbers, barcodes, plus your own custom tags.
- Album art management: view, replace, upload, apply in bulk. Star ratings from 1 to 5.
- Full change history in SQLite with old and new values, and one click revert. Persistent across
  container restarts. History views per song and per folder.
- Built in player with a WaveSurfer.js waveform, click to seek, auto advance, and a collapsible
  sidebar player.
- Three resizable panels: folder tree, song list, detail editor. Sort on any column. Filter by
  text, numeric range, date range or boolean. Show or hide any of 40+ columns. Virtual scrolling
  and infinite pagination for large libraries.
- MusicBrainz lookup with field by field selection of what to apply.
- Bulk editing across many selected songs, with a confirmation summary.
- Mobile first responsive UI with swipe gestures, installable as a PWA.
- Custom playlists, lossless detection, URL based state (bookmark or share any view).
- Multi user authentication with user management built in.
- No telemetry. The only outbound call is to the MusicBrainz API, and only on request.

## Supported audio formats

MP3, FLAC, WAV, AAC, OGG, M4A, M4B, WMA, AIFF, Opus. Lossless formats are detected automatically.
Tags are read with music-metadata and written with node-taglib-sharp. Audio is never re-encoded.

## Install

Docker Compose is the recommended path:

```yaml
services:
  tagr:
    image: ghcr.io/suitux/tagr:latest
    container_name: tagr
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - NODE_ENV=production
      - DATABASE_URL=file:/data/tagr.db
      - AUTH_SECRET=paste-your-generated-secret-here
      - AUTH_USER=admin
      - AUTH_PASSWORD=your-password-here
      - AUTH_URL=https://your-domain.com
    volumes:
      - sqlite_data:/data
      - /path/to/your/music:/music

volumes:
  sqlite_data:
```

Generate the secret with `openssl rand -hex 32`, run `docker compose up -d`, open
http://localhost:3000 and press scan.

A one line Docker run also works:

```
docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v /path/to/music:/music ghcr.io/suitux/tagr:latest
```

Manual install needs Node.js 22 or newer: clone the repo, `pnpm install`, write a `.env`, then
`pnpm build && pnpm start`.

## Configuration

| Variable | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| DATABASE_URL | Yes | SQLite path, for example file:/data/tagr.db |
| AUTH_SECRET | Yes | Signs JWT sessions. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32 |
| AUTH_USER | Yes | Initial account username |
| AUTH_PASSWORD | Yes | Initial account password |
| AUTH_URL | No | Public URL, needed behind a reverse proxy |
| MUSIC_FOLDERS | No | Restricts scanning to specific subdirectories. Defaults to /music |
| PUID, PGID | No | User and group the container runs as. Match the owner of your music files |

Tagr scans /music recursively, so mounting several host paths as subdirectories under /music is
enough to pick them all up.
